entities.summary: Radelgar of Benevento was the prince of Benevento from 851 until 854, succeeding his father Radelchis I. He married a Beneventa noblewoman named Tasselgarda and ruled during a period of significant political instability in the region. Radelgar's reign was marked by power struggles with neighboring lords and the Byzantine Empire, which exerted significant influence over the region. The Prince of Benevento played a minor role in the broader politics of the Mediterranean, with occasional interactions with the Carolingian Empire. Despite his limited influence, Radelgar's legacy is still recognized today as a member of the House of Benevento, a prominent noble family in medieval Italy. The Benevento dynasty would go on to produce several notable rulers, including Guy I and Landulf II, who would play significant roles in shaping the region's history. Radelgar's reign also saw the construction of several important infrastructure projects, including the renovation of the city's cathedral and the expansion of the prince's palace. The legacy of Radelgar of Benevento serves as a testament to the enduring power of the House of Benevento, a testament to the enduring legacy of the medieval Italian nobility.
